protocol.scope: Foundation only: prediction and context reuse; no general reasoning or long-horizon task-success claim
protocol.learner_interface: predict(x) then observe(x,y); context IDs supplied only to the labeled oracle upper bound
protocol.comparisons: Same experience stream and one optimizer update per batch; not claimed equal FLOPs. Count inference over all experts and replay training inputs.
failure_rules: No oracle task IDs in non-oracle arms
No test outcomes for learning or checkpoint selection
Report all seeds, failures, costs and capacity escapes
Do not tune this protocol after seeing registered outcomes; use a separately named follow-up
protocol.relation_to_e1: Exploratory follow-up after E1. E1 code and outputs remain unchanged.
protocol.hypothesis: Protecting persistent models during context identification improves return-task performance without oracle task IDs
protocol.cost_rules: Same observations and optimizer updates; count all model scoring, temporary parameters and peak tensor state; do not claim equal FLOPs
protocol.success_scope: Ablations and stronger controls for the same synthetic family. Not independent evidence of general intelligence or closed-loop long-horizon success.
adversarial_followups_required: many contexts and exhausted module capacity
hypotheses: E2 benefit persists against a context-replay network with approximately the same parameter count as four modules
Copying temporary updates into the source module destroys useful retention
Testing the active module before scoring alternatives lowers routing work without materially increasing error
protocol.resource_control_scope: Width 118 yields 19,828 parameters, versus 19,984 for four 64-wide modules. This is approximate parameter matching only: replay bytes and gradient work differ and must be reported. The compact buffer arm reduces total storage but cannot be assumed exactly matched before its costs are measured.
protocol.isolation_ablation: After each temporary update, overwrite the source persistent module weights and optimizer with the temporary state. Keep all E2 thresholds and selection/commit code unchanged. This specifically removes protection while adaptation is unresolved; resulting module counts may change.
protocol.routing_intervention: When no temporary model exists, score the active model on the observed target. If below the existing E2 reuse threshold, train it and skip other models. Otherwise run the original E2 rule, counting the repeated active score. This trades best-model search for a cheap acceptance test.
